questions.stem: These PA and lateral chest radiographs show an arrow pointing to blunting of the costophrenic angle with a fluid meniscus. What does this finding indicate?

explanation.summary: Blunting of the normally sharp costophrenic angle with a meniscus of dependent fluid on PA and lateral films is the classic radiographic sign of a pleural effusion.

questions.stem: A trauma patient with a chest tube has this sagittal CT angiogram at the aortic isthmus. Injury at this location classically results from what mechanism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chronic hypertension eroding the ascending aorta

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rapid deceleration shearing the relatively fixed aortic isthmus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bacterial seeding of the aortic wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: Atherosclerotic plaque rupture in the coronary sinus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Congenital coarctation of the descending aorta
